{"body": "The account is a pure fold from a multiset of immutable event records to a snapshot; delivery multiplicity and order never enter the result except through the reducer's idempotence and the reducer's choice of latest revision.

Mechanism. (1) Deduplicate deliveries structurally: each record is immutable and a booking/revision pair has at most one content, so duplicates collapse via structural equality. unique preserves first-occurrence order but only membership matters here, since order is discarded next. (2) Group surviving records by booking. (3) For each booking reduce its records by max revision: revision is an integer and a strictly higher revision supersedes ALL lower revisions, so max_by(revision) yields exactly the latest event regardless of arrival sequence. Uniqueness of content per (booking,revision) makes this deterministic. (4) Classify the latest event: if kind == release, the booking reserves 0; if kind == hold, it reserves its quantity exactly when expires_at > now and 0 otherwise. Quantity is the absolute quantity of that booking version, never a delta, so no accumulation is needed and no subtraction can corrupt it. (5) Union the latest events' item names with all stock item names, sort ascending, and for each item sum the active latest quantities (sum over the empty set is 0) and emit {"item":NAME,"reserved":TOTAL,"available":CAPACITY-TOTAL}. Stock items with no events naturally get reserved 0 and available = capacity.

Why replay, reordering, expiry, and cancellation interact correctly. Replay: the dedup step is idempotent, so any finite number of redeliveries yields the same surviving set. Reordering: the only order-sensitive step is selecting the latest revision; max revision is a commutative, associative, total reduction, so input order is irrelevant, and delivery order never appears in the output. Expiry: expiry is decided by comparing the latest event's expires_at to input.now, not by which records arrived; an expired latest hold contributes 0 and, crucially, does not resurrect an older unexpired hold, because older revisions were already superseded before expiry was evaluated. Cancellation: a later revision of kind release supersedes earlier holds and reserves 0; it does not delete the booking, so no rejection ordering is invented, no booking is silently discarded, and the released quantity simply frees capacity. Oversubscription is never clamped: if the sum of active latest quantities exceeds capacity, available is capacity - total and may be negative, which the arithmetic expresses directly.

Assumptions. Revisions, quantities, capacities, and now are integers; a booking has one immutable item; a (booking,revision) pair has a single content; every event item is a listed stock item; revision comparison is meaningful across all events of one booking. If any of these fail (e.g. two contents for one booking/revision, a non-listed item, or a fractional quantity), the fold is undefined and execution failure is the honest outcome.

Falsifiers. The account is defeated by: (a) two records sharing a (booking,revision) with different quantity/kind/item; (b) a latest release still contributing quantity; (c) an expired latest hold allowing an older unexpired hold to reappear; (d) a duplicate delivery changing reserved; (e) delivery order changing the output; (f) available being clamped at zero under oversubscription; (g) omitting a stock item with no events. Any one of these observed would falsify the account.

What a revision preserves. A higher revision preserves the booking's identity and supersession semantics: it replaces all lower revisions while preserving the property that exactly one latest event determines the booking's contribution, and it preserves the invariant that lower revisions never influence the snapshot. messages.content:
You fill one artifact. Return JSON only, carrying "body" and "commitments", both strings. "body" is what you have to say. "commitments" is what you are committing to if it is taken up. If evidence blocks are listed, you may add "citations": each names a block id and quotes that block's own words exactly.
Return one JSON object conforming to: {"properties": {"about": {"items": {"type": "string"}, "type": "array"}, "answers": {"items": {"type": "string"}, "type": "array"}, "body": {"type": "string"}, "citations": {"items": {"properties": {"block": {"minLength": 1, "type": "string"}, "quote": {"minLength": 1, "type": "string"}}, "required": ["block", "quote"], "type": "object"}, "type": "array"}, "commitments": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["body", "commitments"], "type": "object"}

Build an executable account of a replicated stock-reservation snapshot.
Deliveries are an unordered bag of immutable event records. The same record may be delivered
many times. Each booking has exactly one immutable item. For each booking, a strictly higher
integer revision replaces ALL lower revisions. A booking/revision pair never has conflicting
contents. The latest revision may be a hold or release. A latest hold is active exactly when
expires_at > input.now; a latest release reserves zero. An expired latest hold does NOT make an
older unexpired hold reappear. Revision order, not delivery order, determines the latest event.
Quantity is the total quantity of that booking version, never an incremental delta.
Stock is input.stock, a list of {item, capacity}; item names are unique. Events only name
listed stock items. Produce a list in ascending item-name order, including items with no events:
[{"item":NAME,"reserved":TOTAL_ACTIVE_LATEST_QUANTITY,"available":CAPACITY-TOTAL},...].
Oversubscription must be visible as negative availability; never clamp, invent rejection order,
or silently discard a booking. Capacity, quantities, revisions, and logical times are integers.
The task is to derive one general procedure from these obligations, not memorize examples.
Explain why replay, reordering, expiry, and later cancellation interact correctly. State what
would falsify your account and which previously successful behavior a revision preserves.

Write a JSON expression program in the commitments string, optionally wrapped as
{"program": EXPR}. The body is unrestricted prose: explain the mechanism, assumptions,
which observations would defeat it, and what successful behavior a change must preserve.
An expression is a JSON literal (numbers, strings, booleans, null, lists), {"var":"name"},
or an operation object. Literal dictionaries use {"op":"object","fields":{"key":EXPR}}.
Input is {"var":"input"}. The available operations and exact fields are:
get: value EXPR, key EXPR, optional default EXPR (missing keys otherwise fail).
if: test EXPR, then EXPR, else EXPR (only selected branch evaluates).
let: name STRING, value EXPR, do EXPR (lexical scope).
map/filter: items EXPR, as STRING, do EXPR (filter do is boolean).
flatmap: same fields; do returns a list; concatenate the lists.
unique: items EXPR (first occurrence order; values compared structurally).
sort: items EXPR (ascending numbers or strings).
max_by/min_by: items EXPR, as STRING, key EXPR (first tie wins; empty fails).
sum/len/not: value EXPR. sum takes a list of numbers; len a list/string/dictionary.
add/sub/mul/eq/ne/lt/le/gt/ge/and/or/in: args [EXPR, EXPR]. Arithmetic takes numbers
only (never booleans, strings, or lists). Boolean operations and if require booleans.
and/or short circuit. Output values must match the task's declared JSON types exactly.
list: items [EXPR,...] (ordinary JSON lists also evaluate their elements).
Every field is exact: no Python, string interpolation, implicit lambdas, or unknown operators.
Programs are limited to 30,000 expression/collection work units, 100 nesting levels,
4,000 syntax nodes, 4,096 items per collection, 256-bit integers and finite floats,
and 20,000 expanded output nodes. Errors are
execution failures, not refutations of prose. Do not encode the supplied examples as a lookup.

Public examples:
[
  {
    "name": "empty_and_unused_stock",
    "input": {
      "now": 10,
      "stock": [
        {
          "item": "z",
          "capacity": 3
        },
        {
          "item": "a",
          "capacity": 8
        }
      ],
      "events": []
    },
    "expected": [
      {
        "item": "a",
        "reserved": 0,
        "available": 8
      },
      {
        "item": "z",
        "reserved": 0,
        "available": 3
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "name": "duplicate_delivery_is_not_extra_stock",
    "input": {
      "now": 10,
      "stock": [
        {
          "item": "widget",
          "capacity": 10
        }
      ],
      "events": [
        {
          "booking": "b",
          "revision": 1,
          "kind": "hold",
          "quantity": 3,
          "expires_at": 20,
          "item": "widget"
        },
        {
          "booking": "b",
          "revision": 1,
          "kind": "hold",
          "quantity": 3,
          "expires_at": 20,
          "item": "widget"
        },
        {
          "booking": "b",
          "revision": 1,
          "kind": "hold",
          "quantity": 3,
          "expires_at": 20,
          "item": "widget"
        }
      ]
    },
    "expected": [
      {
        "item": "widget",
        "reserved": 3,
        "available": 7
      }
    ]
  }
]
